newsitem.title: USA: Oakmark fund still likes consumer stocks - Barrons.
newsitem.headline: Oakmark fund still likes consumer stocks - Barrons.

text.p: Oakmark Fund manager Robert Sanborn would continue to focus on large capitalization consumer stocks and financial industry names, while shying from the high-technology sector, Barron's said.
"I like businesses that are easy to understand and where the products don't change much over time," Sanborn told the investor weekly newspaper in its December 16 edition.
He liked staples like Philip Morris, Anheuser-Busch Inc, H.J. Heinz Co and American Brands Inc, as well as credit card issuer First USA, Mellon Bank Corp and Torchmark Corp insurance, Barron's said.
He said the revival of the financial stocks still had further to go, Barron's said.

The newspaper said Sanborn was a value investor who liked to buy stocks at 60 percent of their asset or "private market" value. Then he waited for stock price and asset values to converge, the paper said.
Sanborn also said Black & Decker Corp was a compelling play on globalization, according to Barron's.
